code: hb_blob_t *blob = hb_blob_create ((const char *)data, size, HB_MEMORY_MODE_READONLY, NULL, NULL);
note: The fuzzer-provided raw TrueType/OpenType bytes are wrapped as a HarfBuzz blob without copying or trusted-size normalization.
The attacker-controlled blob becomes the source face whose table directory, loca, glyf, and cmap data drive subsetting.
The glyph accelerator reads loca and glyf table blobs from the untrusted face and derives glyph count and glyf length from their blob lengths.
For each retained glyph, untrusted loca offsets select a byte range in the glyf table, then remove_padding may shrink end_offset based on glyph contents.

The boundary check treats the flag/coordinate stream as invalid when two bytes remain, although a simple glyph can legally have no coordinate bytes after its instruction-length field; this rejects a valid trimmed range.
The computed output glyf size is based on the accepted or rejected glyph ranges and later controls the heap allocation size for the subset glyf table.
The subset glyf buffer is heap-allocated with the size calculated from the untrusted glyph ranges.
The writer repeats the untrusted range derivation before copying each glyph into the output buffer.
The final memcpy reads from the attacker-controlled glyf table range into the heap subset buffer; malformed glyph range accounting can make this read extend beyond the allocated source blob.
